does go modules allow some replace magic to keep the imports in all files as `k8s.io/klog` (avoiding huge diff), but the underlying import to be `k8s.io/klog/v2`?

> does go modules allow some replace magic to keep the imports in all files as `k8s.io/klog` (avoiding huge diff), but the underlying import to be `k8s.io/klog/v2`?

Definitely not. The klog API changed in v2 and all references must update to the new import to use it.

swept updates, mechanics look reasonable to me

as part of the release note for 1.19, I would expect us to provide guidance for consumers of k8s components:
1. how to update their main() func to switch to klog/v2 setup
2. if they have other dependencies out of their control that are still logging to klog/v1, how to funnel those klog/v1 calls to klog/v2 (sort of what https://github.com/kubernetes/klog/pull/142 is doing, but I would go in the opposite direction and push them to update the code under their control to klog/v2, and set up a klog v1 -> v2 shim to capture log output from legacy dependencies)

issue_context.body:
As part of Structured Logging effort we will be upgrading klog to version 2. This issue will propose plan for upgrading all dependencies and be used to maintain progress.

Part of https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1602

Plan:
* [x] Cut klog release 2.0.0 (@dims)
* [x] Send PRs to k/k dependencies upgrading klog (taken from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/89717#issuecomment-608091112)
  * [x] k8s.io/gengo (@dims, https://github.com/kubernetes/gengo/pull/173)
  * [x] k8s.io/utils (@dims, https://github.com/kubernetes/utils/pull/152)
  * [x] k8s.io/kube-openapi (@tanjunchen, https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/pull/192)
  * [x] github.com/google/cadvisor (@dims, https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/2478)
  * [x] github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/k8s-cloud-provider (@tanjunchen. https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/k8s-cloud-provider/pull/37, https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/k8s-cloud-provider/pull/38)
  * [x] sigs.k8s.io/apiserver-network-proxy (@tanjunchen, https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/apiserver-network-proxy/pull/100)
  * [x] k8s.io/repo-infra (@dims, https://github.com/kubernetes/repo-infra/pull/185)
* [x] [Optional] Run scalability tests on draft PR to check for performance regressions (@tosi3k)
* [x] Get approval from root owners & schedule upgrade (@dims)
* [x] Send announcement kubernetes-dev@ (@dims)
* [x] Execute the upgrade (@dims)

I ran a test job with the experiment and the test passed. Looking at the dashboards I noticed a few changes:
* Clusterloader
LIST calls for pods in the namespace scope take more time on average than before change (1.63s vs. 3.59s),
* kube-apiserver
slightly higher variance of memory allocation for kube-apiserver (but the memory usage stays the same on average),

Overall, the results look good (at least from my novice perspective).

Dashboard with metrics before the change: [link](http://35.226.146.156:3000/d/uzJNy03Wk/master-dashboard?orgId=1) (source: `grafana-prom`).
Dashboard with metrics after the change: [link](http://35.226.146.156:3000/d/uzJNy03Wk/master-dashboard?orgId=1&var-source=klogv2-experiment&var-etcd_type=All&var-etcd_operation=All&var-verb=All&var-resource=All) (source: `klogv2-experiment`).
@mm4tt does this look ok for you?

Thanks, @tosi3k!

The latency of the pod lists seems suspicious, but my intuition says it's a red herring, most likely coming from the different setup of the test runs. The CI/CD test uses configuration than the manual test. For manual test, we used our scalability prow instance, it's likely that the cl2 was run in different region than the cluster, which could affect the pod list (IIRC, cl2 is the main issuer of these calls).

So yes, to summarize it looks ok. We don't see any obvious scalability blockers for klogv2.
Thanks @dims for all great work!
